files.why: New identity slice: framework-free Role union ('finance' | ...) and CurrentUser entity — the actor concept does not exist yet anywhere.
Pure predicate hasRole(user, role) so 'is finance' is a testable rule, not an inline string compare in a component.
Zod DTO + schema for the /api/me (session) response the role must come from.
Map the session DTO to the core CurrentUser so DTO shapes never leak upward.
fetchCurrentUser() query hitting the session endpoint via httpTransport.
Cached reactive current-user store (role read by many views), mirroring billing/data/store.ts.
MSW handler for /api/me returning a role, so the MSW-mocked dev/test app has a current user.
UI-facing composable exposing role/hasRole; also satisfies the slice's required ui/ presence.
Structural requirement: every slice has routes.ts (empty array here) re-exported by index.ts.
The only public surface: export hasRole/useCurrentUser, mock handlers, and routes for cross-slice use.
Register 'identity' in the slices array — the single source of truth from which every boundary config is generated (CODEOWNERS/arch-review file).
Combine canVoid(invoice) with a finance-role check from @slices/identity (the canonical cross-slice pattern) into canVoidInvoice.
Compose identity's mock handlers into the app-level MSW bootstrap alongside billing/scheduling.

uncertain: Whether identity/role deserves its own slice vs living in shared/. I chose a slice because session/role is application state with its own reason-to-change and 'role/finance' is not one of the banned domain nouns; but shared/ is described as zero-domain-knowledge primitives, so this could go either way and it's an architecture-review call.

Where the 'finance may void' predicate belongs: I kept the role+status composition in billing's UI composable (like worked example 2). It could instead be a pure canVoid(invoice, role) in billing/core/policy.ts, but that would make billing/core depend on identity/core's Role type (a sideways core import), which the boundaries disallow — so the composable felt safer.

The generated boundary configs (.oxlintrc.json, apps/web/.dependency-cruiser.generated.json) and possibly the known-violations baseline will change when a slice is added, but those are regenerated by scripts/generate-configs.ts rather than hand-edited, so I did not list them as manual modifications.

Whether the new slice must ship a non-empty ui/ and routes.ts to pass the structure test (exactly-5-entries rule); an empty routes array + a single composable under ui/ should satisfy it, but I couldn't fully confirm the test's minimums without reading it.
questions: Where does the current user's role actually come from at runtime? There's no auth/session today — is there a real /api/me (or JWT/claims) endpoint to fetch it from, or is standing up that source part of this ticket?

Is UI-only hiding sufficient, or must voiding also be enforced server-side? Hiding the button is presentation; the real authorization guard belongs on the void mutation/endpoint, which is out of this frontend repo's reach.
What is the full role set and its shape (single role vs multiple roles/permissions)? That decides whether Role is a union or a permission set and how hasRole is modeled.

Adding a slice edits architecture.config.ts, which is CODEOWNERS-protected and normally off-limits to feature work — is spinning up a new 'identity' slice pre-approved, or should this ride on an existing slice/shared to avoid architecture review?
What should the UI do while the current user/role is still loading or if the fetch fails — hide the button by default (fail-closed)?
